name: Bekal Fort
tagline: Kerala’s largest seaside fort with sweeping Arabian Sea views
summary: Seventeenth-century Bekal Fort in Kasaragod is Kerala’s largest and best‑preserved fort, set on a dramatic coastal headland next to Bekal Beach. A top heritage and photo spot.
description: Bekal Fort is a 17th‑century laterite fortress built by the Nayakas of Keladi (commonly dated to 1650) that sits on a 40‑acre headland at Pallikkare, Kasaragod. Almost three quarters of its exterior meets the sea; its bastions, observation tower and zigzag entrance give excellent coastal views.

The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) manages the monument; excavations and finds show Mysorean and colonial phases in its history and later additions (including work attributed to Tipu Sultan). The fort has become an iconic location for films and photography.

Visitors come for history, long sea views, sunsets and the adjoining Bekal Beach Park. The fort area connects easily with local beach amenities and the Bekal International Beach Festival (held at Bekal Beach Park in recent years).
Practical details (entry fee, opening hours, guided tours) can change — confirm before you travel with ASI or Kerala Tourism.
highlights: Largest and best‑preserved fort in Kerala, built c.1650
Keyhole‑style headland: bastions and sea‑facing observation tower
Panoramic Arabian Sea views and sunset photography
Close to Bekal Beach Park and beach festival events
Managed and conserved by the Archaeological Survey of India

sections.heading: Background
body: Bekal Fort was begun by Nayaka rulers of Ikkeri/ Keladi and completed around 1650. Its strategic position on the Malabar coast made it important during the Nayaka, Mysore (Hyder Ali/Tipu Sultan) and later British periods. Archaeological work and finds reflect its long maritime and military role.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Walk the ramparts and visit the central observation tower for sweeping coastal views and photo vantage points. Look for cannons, storage‑tanks and the zigzag entrance and defensive holes in the walls — features that explain its naval defence design.

Combine the fort with a stroll along Bekal Beach Park, local kite and sand‑sculpture displays during the beach festival, and nearby village experiences promoted by Kerala’s Responsible Tourism mission (cashew units, fishing, toddy‑tapping demonstrations).

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Bekal is about 10–20 km from local railheads (Kanhangad, Kasaragod) and roughly 70–100 km from the nearest airports (Mangalore ~71 km, Kannur ~101 km; distances depend on route). The site is managed by ASI — check ASI or Kerala Tourism for current opening times, entry rules and any conservation closures before you go.

Facilities near the fort include parking, beach park amenities and local eateries in Bekal and Pallikkara; if you plan to attend festival events (December has hosted the Bekal International Beach Festival) check event dates and crowd guidance in advance.

latest.text: PIB: HAL, National Culture Fund and ASI signed an MoA to support conservation and site‑development works at several monuments including Bekal Fort; HAL committed in‑principle funding for site improvements under ASI guidance.
HAL CSR project list (FY 2026‑27) includes a multi‑year plan for Bekal Fort: restoration of moat and fortification walls plus visitor amenities (line item and funding included).
Archaeological Survey of India (Thrissur Circle) issued a 2025‑26 tender for conservation works at Bekal Fort (historic restoration and maintenance contracts), showing active ASI maintenance work.
Local media reported the return/organisation of the Bekal International Beach Festival (planned for late December), a recurring 10‑day event held at Bekal Beach Park near the fort.

visitorInfo.bestTime: November–February for dry weather and clear sea views; December for the beach festival (check dates).
visitorInfo.howToReach: Nearest rail: Kanhangad (≈10 km) or Kasaragod (≈16 km); nearest airports: Mangalore (~70–75 km) and Kannur (~100 km). Bekal is on NH‑66; regular buses and taxis connect from Kanhangad/Kasargod. Confirm local connections before travel.
etiquette: The fort is an ASI protected monument — don’t climb on fragile sections; follow signboards and barriers.
Sunset brings the best light for photos but can be crowded; arrive earlier to find a good vantage point.
Facilities and opening hours can change during restoration work or festivals — check ASI/Kerala Tourism before visiting.
Combine the fort with Bekal Beach Park and local village experiences for a fuller day trip.
